analysis.one_liner: CG Power makes transformers, switchgear and motors for power transmission and industry, and is now also betting on semiconductor assembly through a joint venture (CG Semi/Axiro).
analysis.whats_happening: CG Power's board met on 23 October 2026 and approved Q2 FY27 (quarter ended September 2026) results: consolidated revenue rose 30.1% YoY to ₹3,801.54 crore and consolidated PAT rose 44% YoY to ₹409 crore, both records. Standalone order intake jumped 90% YoY and the standalone order backlog reached ₹21,820 crore, up 61% YoY. The board also approved a ₹748 crore greenfield switchgear expansion and a rise in transformer capacity from 15,000 MVA to 40,000 MVA. Despite the strong numbers, the stock fell through the following week amid broad market weakness.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a 24-year-old electrical equipment maker that nearly went to zero in 2019-20 after a promoter-led fraud, was rescued by the Murugappa Group (Tube Investments), and has since rebuilt into a genuinely strong, debt-free, high-return business. The tension: the core business is firing on all cylinders, but the stock trades at roughly 113 times trailing earnings - a price that assumes a lot of future success, including from a semiconductor venture that currently loses money and won't earn any until FY28 or FY29. You are paying up front for a bet that hasn't paid off yet.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 (Sep-26): consolidated revenue ₹3,801.54 crore (+30.1% YoY), consolidated PAT ₹409 crore (+44% YoY), EBITDA margin expanded to 18.2% from 16.4%. Standalone PAT was higher at ₹450 crore (+46% YoY) - the gap versus consolidated is not an accounting distortion but the semiconductor JV's losses being consolidated in; management flagged CG Semi and Axiro together created about ₹35 crore of 'investment drag' (91 bps of margin) this quarter. Power Systems sales grew 48% YoY with margin expansion, while the Industrial segment (motors, railways) fell 2% YoY - management said this was a deliberate choice to walk away from low-margin railway orders and unpassed-on commodity cost inflation rather than chase volume. No formal revenue guidance was given; management guided to ~₹1,000 crore of core capex in FY27 and ₹700-800 crore in FY28.
analysis.performance_read: Over 5 years the stock is up 455% against the Nifty's 23.8% and peer ABB's 250%, but this window starts after the business had already been rescued - it does not capture the near-total wealth destruction investors suffered when the stock fell from roughly ₹225 (2014, pre-split-adjusted terms vary by source) to around ₹5 by March 2020 following the Avantha-era fraud. That collapse, and the subsequent change of promoter, is the real story behind today's low base; investors who held through 2019 lost almost everything before the turnaround began. The current -15.3% pullback from the July 2026 peak of ₹976.5 is an ordinary drawdown, not a crash, and is unrelated to any corporate action - the listed splits (2006, 2006, 2010) are all historical and don't affect this period's return readings.
analysis.valuation_read: Expensive by every conventional yardstick: trailing P/E of roughly 113-117x versus a 3-year average near 65x, and a price-to-book of about 17x. Why it is expensive is clear - the market is paying for both an unusually profitable core business (ROCE ~28%, zero debt) and for optionality in the CG Semi/Axiro semiconductor bet, whose commercial payoff management itself says is not expected before FY28-29. Whether that price is justified is a separate question this report cannot answer - it depends entirely on execution of a business that doesn't yet generate revenue.
analysis.growth_read: Growth this quarter was both margin-led and volume-led in the Power Systems segment (sales +48% YoY with 180 bps of margin expansion), which is the more durable combination. The Industrial segment (motors, railways) shrank 2% YoY, a volume decline management chose deliberately to protect margins against price competition and unrecovered commodity costs - worth watching if it persists rather than reverses.
analysis.health_read: Financial risk is minimal: debt-to-equity is just 0.01, so the company is effectively debt-free, and ROE (20.4%) and ROCE (~28%) are both well above peer medians. The real risk here is business/execution risk, not balance-sheet risk - specifically whether the capital being poured into the semiconductor JV (₹1,000 crore of core capex guided for FY27 alone) converts into profit on the timeline management expects. Whether reported profit is converting cleanly into operating cash flow was not verified - check this on Screener.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Tube Investments of India (Murugappa Group) holds about 56.3% and has confirmed zero pledged shares through FY26, a sharp contrast with the previous promoter (Avantha Group/Gautam Thapar), whose pledged shares were seized by lenders in 2019 after the fraud was uncovered. Institutional ownership is broad - FIIs around 11-12%, DIIs around 19%, mutual funds near 9.4-9.9% (top holders include Axis ELSS Tax Saver, ICICI Prudential Large & Mid Cap, Motilal Oswal Flexi Cap) and LIC at 2.12%. PE firm KKR, which once controlled roughly 21% after enforcing the Avantha pledge, has fully exited over time. There is no marquee individual investor on the register - ownership is promoter- and institution-dominated.
strengths: Debt-free balance sheet (debt-to-equity of 0.01) with ROCE around 28%, well above the sector median of ~20%
Consolidated revenue up 30.1% YoY and EBITDA margin expanding from 16.4% to 18.2% in Q2 FY27
Standalone order backlog of ₹21,820 crore, up 61% YoY, giving several quarters of revenue visibility
Promoter (Murugappa Group) holding of 56.3% carries zero pledge, a clean structure versus the prior promoter
watchpoints: Trailing P/E of roughly 113-117x is well above the stock's own 3-year average of ~65x, leaving little room for disappointment
CG Semi/Axiro semiconductor JV is a quarterly profit drag (~₹35 crore this quarter) with no commercial revenue expected before FY28-29
Industrial segment (railways, motors) sales fell 2% YoY on project deferments and unrecovered commodity costs - a margin-over-volume trade that needs to reverse into growth eventually
The company's own history includes a near-total promoter-fraud collapse in 2019-20; the current clean governance record is only about five years old
analysis.one_thing: Whether the CG Semi/Axiro semiconductor fab reaches commercial production on the guided FY28-FY29 timeline and turns from a ~₹35 crore quarterly drag into a profit contributor - that is what would justify today's ~113x earnings multiple.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue (₹3,801.54 crore, +30.1% YoY) and PAT (₹409 crore, +44% YoY) were cross-checked across Business Standard, Tradebrains and Motilal Oswal and are consistent. The higher standalone PAT figure (₹450 crore, +46% YoY) reported elsewhere is not a contradiction but reflects JV losses dragging down the consolidated number - flagged explicitly above. P/E estimates ranged 112x-117x across sources; the cluster was used. Operating cash flow versus reported PAT was not verified - check on Screener. Pre-2020 un-adjusted share price levels (₹225 in 2014, ₹5 in 2020) came from a single source and should be treated as directional, not exact.
